rootCause.primary: GeoCeDGActionRegistry.openDiagnostic assumes a JDK/JRE filesystem contract (<java.home>/bin/javaw.exe or java). It holds for a Gradle/IDE JDK and never for the jpackage runtime, which jlink builds with --strip-native-commands; the fallback name 'java' does not exist there either.
rootCause.introducedBy: b49219408 (2026-09-04, G9U1); every packaged build since then carries it; consistent with the author's mid-September reproduction

additionalFindingsInTheSameSeam.summary: the child is started with ProcessBuilder defaults (stdout/stderr pipes) and the parent never reads them; Classic logs to the console through LoggerD, fills the pipe and blocks before showing its window
additionalFindingsInTheSameSeam.evidence: dev route, unmodified product code: Laboratory with Templatev7.ggb blocks (main thread in FileOutputStream.writeBytes <- LoggerD.print:168); scratch packaged secondary launcher: same file blocks with pipes and loads (23 construction steps) with Redirect.DISCARD
affects: Open Classic diagnostic session (any session that logs enough)

additionalFindingsInTheSameSeam.summary: the development child receives none of the four declared JVM options (--add-exports x3, --enable-native-access) that runGeoCeDG and package.yml declare; a packaged general java route would lose them too and would also lose jpackage.app-path

candidateC.name: relaunch GeoCeDG.exe with an explicit mode argument
candidateC.analysis: feasible in principle (GeoCeDG.main parses arguments before any profile initialization), but it widens the product entry point and the .cedg open-verb target with a Classic mode, gives both processes the same executable identity, still needs the development fallback, and needs product code in the entry point; no packaging change

candidateD.result: no further viable candidate found: in-process Classic violates the separate-process requirement; JNI/jvm.dll launching is not a supported contract; PATH/environment discovery would select an arbitrary JVM
